args.title: Fix weekly scheduled exports skipping their first run
args.body:
File: src/export/scheduler.ts

In `nextRunAt`, the `daily` case correctly checks whether the computed run time (today at `RUN_HOUR_UTC`) has already passed before deciding to advance by a day: `if (next <= from) next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 1);`. The `weekly` case skips this check entirely and always does `next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 7)`, regardless of whether the run-hour slot on the current day has already elapsed.

Because this same function is used to compute the first run for a brand-new weekly schedule, a schedule created before `RUN_HOUR_UTC` (e.g. 05:40 UTC, before the 06:00 UTC run hour) should fire that same day, but instead is pushed a full week out — matching the reported behaviour where the first scheduled email never arrives and the series only starts the following Monday. Daily schedules don't show this problem because they already have the "has this slot passed?" guard.

Proposed fix: mirror the daily branch's guard in the weekly case, e.g.:

```
case "weekly":
  if (next <= from) next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 7);
  break;
```

This way, if the run-hour slot for the current day hasn't passed yet, the next (first) run stays on the current day; otherwise it correctly advances a full week, preserving the intended weekly cadence for subsequent runs.
